answer_1.quote: Table-to-text generation or insight generation ... is a challenging task in natural language generation (NLG), where a NLG system generates insights from a data table.
answer_1.outputs: textual insights summarizing the contents of tables

answer_2.quote: We use the standard reference-free automatic metrics for the LogicNLG benchmark –trained table entailment metrics TAPAS and TAPEX. We focus on TAPEX in the paper... TAPAS as well as scores for other generation aspects are given in Appendix B (self-BLEU, unique tokens and Shannon entropy to measure diversity, percentage of failures, and the average output lengths).

answer_3.quote: We also ran an LLM-as-a-judge evaluation with the Llama 3.3 70B model. We crafted the prompt to be as close as possible to the annotation instructions for human evaluators.
methods: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation using a prompt modeled on human annotation instructions

answer_4.quote: We run a crowdsourced human evaluation on a sample of our data (50 tables from each benchmark) with outputs from four LLMs... We ask the annotators to spot and highlight accuracy errors in the insights on the word level, following Kasner and Dusek (2024)'s setup. We operate with four error categories: incorrect, not checkable, misleading, and other.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators spot and highlight accuracy errors in the generated insights, categorising each error as incorrect, not checkable, misleading, or other.
